title: SAFFIRE I-III: the fire they let grow
voice: the brave test: it burned on purpose

core.quote: The objectives of SAFFIRE-II are to determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and to investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.

hook: They lit a large fire in space on purpose. It rode in the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it left the station while cameras watched.
reveal: Saffire set out to test how fast a large fire grows in low-gravity, using separate pieces of Sibal fabric, silicone, structure PMMA, flat PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex in a flow duct with fans moving air past them while cameras and heat sensors watched.
bridge: Knowing how fabric burns in moving air with low gravity helps us think about what air is safe to breathe in a Moon home.

engineer.text: The experiment set out to measure how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low gravity and to compare low gravity flammability limits with those from NASA normal gravity screening.
engineer.quote: The objectives of SAFFIRE-II are to determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and to investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.

title: BASS: does Earth's test tell the truth?

core.quote: Begin to bridge the gap between the normal gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test#1 method, ground-based microgravity tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity.

hook: Could ground tests be missing how things really burn in space, so the team planned to begin to bridge the gap with longer burns in flight.
reveal: The plan was to burn fabric and other shapes inside a glove box on the space station, lighting one end with a wire while a fan pushed air with or against the flame, and watch size, shape, color, spread and quenching.
bridge: This work is not about Moon base air, but about how fabrics burn and how gas can put them out when air moves in space.

engineer.text: This investigation set out to bridge ground-based flammability tests and actual material flammability in microgravity by watching flames burn for longer times in flight.
engineer.quote: Begin to bridge the gap between the normal gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test#1 method, ground-based microgravity tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity.

title: BASS-II: a gentle breeze is enough

core.quote: Study the ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity.

hook: It might be surprising that air barely moving in weightlessness is worth studying, and scientists wanted to see how such gentle flows relate to flames starting, growing, and going out.
reveal: Astronauts worked as lab partners with a small wind tunnel inside a glovebox on the space station, testing fuel samples in slow flows going with and against the flame while changing airflow and oxygen by adding nitrogen, and watching how flames looked and spread.
bridge: Learning how slow air and oxygen levels relate to burning helps plan how to spot and stop fires in places like a Moon base where people live and breathe.

engineer.text: The study set out to contribute to combustion computational models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth.
engineer.quote: BASS-II results contribute to the combustion computational models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth.

title: FLEX: putting fire out in space

core.quote: The FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) investigation aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity environments, measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6, and develop reliable predictive models for combustion limits under reduced gravity conditions.

hook: Think like a firefighter learning to smother a floating fire. Flex will map when liquid fuel can burn and test gases meant to put flames out.
reveal: The plan will light fuel droplets and watch how they burn and fade, then try again with lowered oxygen and with smothering gases nearby to map when flames can stay lit and when they go out.
bridge: This matters for Moon-base air because knowing what oxygen lets fuel keep burning helps shape cabin air and rules for putting fires out.

engineer.text: This investigation aims to map when liquid fuels can burn in weightlessness and test how well different gas suppressants can put those flames out to help improve fire safety procedures for future missions.
engineer.quote: These investigations are essential for advancing the fundamental understanding of combustion processes in microgravity and enhancing fire safety protocols for future space missions.

title: FLEX-2: fuels like the real thing

core.quote: The primary goal of the FLEX-2 flight experiments is to extend the results of FLEX-1 to fuels and environmental conditions that mimic real combustor conditions, as well as, provide benchmark experimental data on bi-component droplet combustion over a wide range of initial conditions in order to validate numerical simulations and to develop new theoretical models.

hook: As an engineer, I want fuels that act like what we use in a real combustor. So we set out to watch how tiny mixed fuel drops burn.
reveal: We filled a chamber with chosen gas mixes, placed drops of fuel, let them settle, then lit them and watched the flame with cameras while tracking heat and pressure.
bridge: To be clear, this test is about engine-like burning, not about the air we would breathe in a Moon home.

title: CFI: flames that burn cold

core.quote: Analyze the effects of helium dilution on cool flame behavior.

hook: What makes a cool flame keep burning, and what makes it go out?
reveal: They hung tiny fuel drops between thin needles or on fibers inside a chamber, lit them with a hot wire that pulled back, and used cameras to watch drop size and flame size while changing the gas mix.
bridge: This work is not about Moon-base air, it is about how tiny fuel drops burn cool and make soot.

title: CFI-G: cool flames on demand

core.quote: Plan and support flight testing on the International Space Station (ISS).

hook: Think of this like a recipe book for cool flames that the team plans to test on the space station.
reveal: The plan is to make round flames on the space station with different fuels and air mixes, changing flow and pressure and flame direction, and watching with cameras and heat tools to learn when cool flames could form.
bridge: This study is not about Moon base air but about the basic recipe for when cool flames might appear.

title: Flame Design: a flame without soot

core.quote: Obtain soot-inception limits of quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames as functions of flow rate, Zst, amount of inert (N2 or CO2), and pressure for C2H4 and CH4 flames.

hook: We plan to shape round flames to learn when soot begins to show.
reveal: The team plans to try round flames in drop towers and on the space station using different flows and pressures, and to watch when soot starts and how size and color and heat change with cameras and heat sensors.
bridge: This study is about how round flames form soot, not about the air in a Moon base.

title: BRE: a burner that acts like a solid

core.quote: The BRE flight program seeks to establish the burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties.

hook: I will stand in for solid fuel and will burn in still weightless air while watchers study how I act.
reveal: The team will set the air in the chamber, will start fuel flow and will light it, then will watch the flame without changing flow while the burner will warm, until the flame will fade or the warmth will steady.
bridge: This will help us think about fire safety in air made for crews living in a Moon base.

title: CLD: the faintest flames

core.quote: Characterize the behavior of weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene, as a function of velocity and fuel dilution, through measurement of flame shape, lift-off heights, temperatures and extinction limits.

hook: Come close and listen, for they plan to light very faint flames and watch how they lift and fade.
reveal: They plan to test thin methane and ethylene flames while changing flow and mix, and plan to measure shape, lift, warmth, and where flames go out, plus glow and warmth from soot in smoky flames.
bridge: This study is about something else, as it plans to shape computer models of faint and smoky flames.

title: E-FIELD: steering a flame with electricity

core.quote: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the relationship between electric field voltage and chemi-ion current, analyze the dynamic response of flames to electric field changes, evaluate soot formation, and characterize stabilized near-limit lifted flames.

hook: Who says flames get to do whatever they want. This test talks back and bosses them around with electricity.
reveal: They lit gas flames floating weightless, with and without a soft flow of air around them. Then they switched on a field between the burner and a mesh above and watched how the charged bits in the flame moved it, how soot formed, and how fast it reacted, using cameras and heat sensors.
bridge: This is not about Moon-base air, it is about learning how electricity can push a flame around.

title: s-Flame: the perfect sphere

core.quote: to compare with detailed computational simulation to assess transport properties and detailed chemical kinetics (including chemiluminescence)

hook: Scientists plan to create round flames so they can compare what the flames look like and how they act with detailed computer models.
reveal: They will feed fuel mixes through a round burner and light them, then will measure flame pictures, heat, and light energy to see how flame shape and going-out points match the models.
bridge: This experiment is not about Moon-base air; it is about how round flames act so models can be checked.

title: SLICE: where a flame holds on

core.quote: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity.

hook: Imagine a flame as a climber gripping near the base, trying to hold on while air streams by.
reveal: They lit flames in a fan-blown duct with swap-out burner tubes, tried methane and ethylene and mixes thinned with nitrogen, took still pictures with flow and heat readings laid over them, and the data was analysed to correlate flame shape with steadiness and air motion and fuel type.
bridge: This work is not about Moon-base air, but about how still flames hold on and give off soot and heat in weightlessness.

title: SPICE: when a flame starts to smoke

core.quote: The objective of SPICE is to better understand the complex process of combustion by observing flames in a microgravity environment aboard the International Space Station (ISS) and analogous ground experiments.

hook: As a chemist I watch clean flames turn smoky and ask when and why soot slips free.
reveal: They lit many flames inside a glovebox lab on the space station, using different fuels and air flows, and used still and video cameras to watch flame length and catch the moment each flame began to release soot.
bridge: This work is not about the air in a Moon home, it is about how free-floating flames make soot.

title: SAME / SAME-R: smoke that grows differently

core.quote: One of the major goals of this investigation was to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity and to relate the droplet size distribution to the smoke generation and smoke transport conditions in the experiment.

hook: Something strange was in the air, and the clues were too small to see. The case was to track how big liquid smoke drops get in low gravity.
reveal: The crew set up boxes and cameras to gather clues, made smoke from heated spacecraft material, caught soot for microscope study, and checked how detectors responded.
bridge: For air in a Moon base, the piece of the puzzle here was measuring smoke size and how detectors responded.

title: Ground: why space soot is different

core.quote: The objective of this investigation was to integrate computational and experimental methods to derive temperature distributions and soot volume fractions from the Smoke Point in Coflow Experiment (SPICE) data available in PSI.

hook: Soot from flames behaves very differently on the ground than in weightless space. This work tries to explain what controls that big mismatch.
reveal: They studied flame photos from the Smoke Point in Coflow Experiment to map heat and soot, then built computer models of flow and soot with light reabsorption and soot clumps growing. They ran the models for ground and weightless cases and compared them to the photos to test what matters most.
bridge: This work is not about Moon base air, it is about why sooty flames look different with and without gravity.

title: Ground: modelling flame spread

core.quote: The objective of this research was to develop and validate new flamelet generated manifold (FGM) modeling techniques for concurrent flame spread in microgravity.

hook: I make models that try to copy how fire moves. My job is to make the math behave like real flames do.
reveal: We ran computer copies of flames moving over flat sheets, balls, rods and wax sticks, then checked them against space photos of real Bass flames rebuilt into soot and heat maps to see if flame shape, heat, soot and spread pace matched.
bridge: Knowing which spacecraft stuff can burn helps us guess how fire might act in the air of a Moon home.

engineer.text: This research set out to develop modeling techniques for flame spread to help enable prediction of flammability limits for spacecraft materials and support spacecraft safety and hazard mitigation.
engineer.quote: Ultimately, the long-term goal was to enable accurate prediction of flammability limits for spacecraft materials and to provide a tool that could also serve as a subgrid-scale model in large-eddy simulations of fires, supporting spacecraft safety and hazard mitigation.

title: Ground: what tipped FLEX's cool flames

core.quote: Focusing on both small and large droplets, the work mapped stability windows for ignition, sustained oscillation, transitions to hot ignition and warm-flame behavior, and extinction under microgravity.

hook: We dug into flight data from Flex to learn why some set cool flames kept burning while others died out.
reveal: We built a computer model checked against space measurements, then tested drifting air alone, added heat alone, and both together on small and large drops to map starting, wobbling, warming, and fading.
bridge: This study is not about Moon base air, it is about what tips tiny fuel drops toward lasting cool flames or toward going out.

title: Ground: a new map of flammability

core.quote: Develop a new diagram of the flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion, and convection.

hook: Like a mapmaker tracing faint shores, this work charts where cool flames can linger and where they must fade.
reveal: Using space flame data as a guide, the team ran ground tests and computer models to see how changing air lets cool flames hold on or die out.
bridge: This study is not about Moon base air directly, but about mapping cool flame limits in a broader sense.
